proposals.before: In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong had been enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhan’en was again sent to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit, announce the sacrifice, and install the spirit seat.
proposals.after: In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong had been enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhanzhan was again sent to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit, announce the sacrifice, and install the spirit seat.
proposals.reason: The given name 瞻颭 romanizes as Zhanzhan; Zhan’en does not match the Chinese.

proposals.before: In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhan’en was again dispatched to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit for a sacrificial announcement and to install the spirit seat in peace.
proposals.after: In the first year of Xuande, after Taizong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the Prince of Zheng Zhu Zhanzhan was again dispatched to the Hall of Ancestors to set out wine and fruit for a sacrificial announcement and to install the spirit seat in peace.
proposals.reason: The given name 瞻颭 romanizes as Zhanzhan; Zhan’en does not match the Chinese.

proposals.before: The bier-bearers numbered as many as a thousand, and all along the route they demanded whatever they wished.
proposals.after: The boat-haulers numbered as many as a thousand, and all along the route they demanded whatever they wished.
proposals.reason: 輓夫 on the Nanjing fresh-tribute boats are trackers or haulers, not funeral bier-bearers.

proposals.before: The bearers of the bier reached a thousand men, and along the route they extorted everything.
proposals.after: The boat-haulers reached a thousand men, and along the route they extorted everything.
proposals.reason: 輓夫 on the tribute boats are haulers, not bier-bearers.

proposals.before: In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were transferred to the Jingshen Hall, and those of Wenzong and his empress and the rest to the Yongxiao Hall.
proposals.after: In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were transferred to the Jingshen Hall, and those of the Wen Emperor and his empress and the rest to the Yongxiao Hall.
proposals.reason: Wenhuangdi is Ming Chengzu’s temple designation Emperor Wen, not the later temple name Wenzong.

proposals.before: In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were moved to the Jingshen Hall, and those of Wenzong and his empress and below to the Yongxiao Hall.
proposals.after: In the eighteenth year the death anniversaries of Gaozu and his empress were moved to the Jingshen Hall, and those of the Wen Emperor and his empress and below to the Yongxiao Hall.
proposals.reason: Wenhuangdi is Ming Chengzu’s temple designation Emperor Wen, not Wenzong.

proposals.before: When Xiaozong took the throne, he posthumously honored his mother, Consort Ji, as Empress Xiaomu and enshrined her at Maoling.
proposals.after: When Xiaozong took the throne, he posthumously honored his mother, Consort Ji, as Empress Xiaomu and had her jointly buried at Maoling.
proposals.reason: The verb fuzang means companion burial at the mausoleum, not enshrinement of a spirit tablet.

proposals.before: The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Mencius entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
proposals.after: The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Lady Meng entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
proposals.reason: Mengzi in this Chunqiu argument is Hui Gong’s principal wife, not the philosopher Mencius.

proposals.before: The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Mencius entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
proposals.after: The Spring and Autumn Annals records “the palace of Zhongzi, the younger wife”; Hu Anguo’s commentary says: “When Lady Meng entered Duke Hui’s temple, Zhongzi had no place for sacrifice.”
proposals.reason: Mengzi here is the principal wife in the no-double-matching precedent, not Mencius.

proposals.before: The commentators say: ‘Closest means the mother born to the uncle.’
proposals.after: The commentators say: ‘Closest means the birth mother of the father-in-law (the husband’s father).’
proposals.reason: 舅所生母 in this ritual commentary is the husband’s father’s birth mother (paternal grandmother), not a mother borne by an uncle.

proposals.before: The commentators say: ‘Closest means the mother born to the uncle.’
proposals.after: The commentators say: ‘Closest means the birth mother of the father-in-law (the husband’s father).’
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 舅所生母 in the literal English.

proposals.before: The Grand Mentor Shi Bao and others also said it could not be done.
proposals.after: The Supervisor of the Household Shi Bao and others also said it could not be done.
proposals.reason: 詹事 is the Ming Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent (Zhanshi), not Grand Mentor (太傅).

proposals.before: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Yuan had already been appointed acting vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber and exalted sacrifice to the imperial father in the Grand Temple; Minister of Rites Xi Shu and others deliberated: “The Son of Heaven has seven temples; Zhou Wen and Wu both had merit and virtue, and therefore established the Wen and Wu Eternal Chambers above the three zhao and three mu.
proposals.after: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Yuan had already been appointed vice director of a bureau of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and again memorialized requesting establishment of an Eternal Chamber and exalted sacrifice to the imperial father in the Grand Temple; Minister of Rites Xi Shu and others deliberated: “The Son of Heaven has seven temples; Zhou Wen and Wu both had merit and virtue, and therefore established the Wen and Wu Eternal Chambers above the three zhao and three mu.
proposals.reason: 光祿寺署丞 names the office 署丞; 署 is not the ‘acting’ prefix.

proposals.before: Soon thereafter Left Sublector Jiang Rubi requested moving the imperial father’s temple to the head of the mu temples, to serve as the future Eternal Chamber, standing alongside Chengzu’s temple.
proposals.after: Soon thereafter Left Mentor Jiang Rubi requested moving the imperial father’s temple to the head of the mu temples, to serve as the future Eternal Chamber, standing alongside Chengzu’s temple.
proposals.reason: 左庶子 is Left Mentor (Zuo Shuzi), not ‘Sublector’.

proposals.before: Right Supporter Guo Xiyan also wished, outside Taizu’s temple and Wen’s Eternal Chamber, to establish only four parental temples and remove Xiaozong and Wuzong from the line.
proposals.after: Right Adviser Guo Xiyan also wished, outside Taizu’s temple and Wen’s Eternal Chamber, to establish only four parental temples and remove Xiaozong and Wuzong from the line.
proposals.reason: 右贊善 is Right Adviser (You Zanshan), not ‘Supporter’.

proposals.before: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Nanchang, Huoqiu, Xiaocai, Anfeng, and Huoqiu, and the consorts of Huoqiu and Anfeng, Ladies Zhai and Zhao, should form one altar;
proposals.after: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Nanchang, Huoqiu, Xiacai, and Anfeng, and the consorts of Huoqiu and Anfeng, Ladies Zhai and Zhao, should form one altar;
proposals.reason: Chinese lists four brothers (南昌、霍丘、下蔡、安豐) then two consorts; English invents a fifth ‘Huoqiu’ prince and misspells 下蔡 as Xiaocai rather than Xiacai.

proposals.before: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Nanchang, Huoqiu, Xiaocai, Anfeng, and Huoqiu, and the consorts of Huoqiu and Anfeng, Ladies Zhai and Zhao, should form one altar;
proposals.after: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Nanchang, Huoqiu, Xiacai, and Anfeng, and the consorts of Huoqiu and Anfeng, Ladies Zhai and Zhao, should form one altar;
proposals.reason: Same distortion as the idiomatic line: extra Huoqiu prince not in 皇兄南昌王、霍丘王、下蔡王、安豐王.

proposals.before: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Mengcheng, Xuyi, and Linhuai, and Lady Liu consort of Linhuai, should form one altar—later it was fixed that consorts should all be styled consort princess;
proposals.after: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Mengcheng, Xuyi, and Linhuai, and Lady Liu consort of Linhuai, should form one altar—later it was fixed that all such ladies should be restyled consorts (fei);
proposals.reason: 妃 here restyles 夫人 as princely consorts, not ‘consort princess’.

proposals.before: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Mengcheng, Xuyi, and Linhuai, and Lady Liu consort of Linhuai, should form one altar—later it was fixed that consorts should all be styled consort princess;
proposals.after: the emperor’s elder brothers the Princes of Mengcheng, Xuyi, and Linhuai, and Lady Liu consort of Linhuai, should form one altar—later it was fixed that all such ladies should be restyled consorts (fei);

proposals.before: In the fourteenth year of Wanli, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Pei Yingzhang said: “The princes were originally enshrined as joint offerings of the great-grandfather.
proposals.after: In the fourteenth year of Wanli, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Pei Yingzhang said: “The princes were originally attached as collateral joint offerings to the ancestors.
proposals.reason: 從祖祔食 means collateral/ancillary enshrinement with the ancestors, not specifically ‘the great-grandfather’.

proposals.before: Thereupon the Prince of Jingjiang’s chief steward fully submitted the music sections, and stated that the five sacrifices of the first ten days of the four meng months and New Year’s Eve—the items, stands, dancers, and rites—all followed the founding regulations.”
proposals.after: Thereupon the Prince of Jingjiang’s chief steward fully submitted the music sections, and stated that the five sacrifices of the first ten days of the first month of each season and New Year’s Eve—the items, stands, row-dancers, and rites—all followed the founding regulations.”
proposals.reason: 四孟 means the first month of each of the four seasons, not an untranslated 'meng months'; 佾舞 is the regulated row-dance, not generic dancers.

proposals.before: The chief sacrificer opened the casket and bore each ancestral spirit tablet, installing them in order.
proposals.after: The chief sacrificer opened the casket and bore the spirit tablets of each ancestral grandfather and grandmother, installing them in order.
proposals.reason: 祖妣 names both male and female ancestral tablets; the English drops the female ancestors (妣).

decisions.reason: The Chinese heading is 〈（吉禮六）〉; the English closing 〉 is an unmatched CJK title bracket, and removing it leaves an accurate rendering.
The same stray 〉 appears in the literal field and is not required once （吉禮六） is given in English parentheses.
鄭王瞻颭 names the prince 瞻颭, romanized Zhanzhan; Zhan’en does not match those characters.
The literal line repeats Zhu Zhan’en for 瞻颭; Zhanzhan is the matching romanization.
In the memorial about 南京進鮮船, 輓夫 are the boats’ haulers or trackers, not funeral bier-bearers.
The literal ‘bearers of the bier’ likewise misreads 輓夫 on the tribute-boat route.
文皇帝 is the Wen Emperor (Chengzu’s designation), not the temple name Wenzong.

decisions.reason: The literal Wenzong is the same misidentification of 文皇帝.
祔葬茂陵 is companion burial at Maoling; the following 不得祔廟 shows this is not tablet enshrinement.
In Hu Anguo’s Chunqiu comment, 孟子 is Duke Hui’s principal wife Lady Meng, not the philosopher Mencius.
The literal Mencius is the same error in this no-double-matching precedent.

decisions.after: The Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent Shi Bao and others also said it could not be done.
decisions.reason: 詹事 is the Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, not Grand Mentor; the proposed short title omits the heir-apparent household.
光祿寺署丞 is the assistant director of a bureau in that court; 署 here is the bureau, not an ‘acting’ prefix.
左庶子 is Left Mentor, not the nonce title Sublector.
右贊善 is Right Adviser, not Supporter.
The Chinese names four brothers—南昌王、霍丘王、下蔡王、安豐王—then two consorts; the extra Huoqiu prince is invented and 下蔡 is Xiacai.

claimRevisions.reason: The English personal name Zhu Zhan’en was produced by misreading 瞻颭; the characters romanize as Zhu Zhanzhan.
The given-name value Zhan’en does not match 瞻颭 and should be Zhanzhan.
文皇帝 is the Wen Emperor, not the temple name Wenzong.
孟子 in this Chunqiu citation is Lady Meng, Duke Hui’s principal wife, not Mencius.
